jetset.com A reversal of the trend which was noted before the pandemic, when many English people chose to go further afield to the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. The pandemic has accelerated the shift, and the threat of a low number of visitors or a weak economy has meant that local tourist attractions have thrived. Many British people are discovering their love of local culture and scenery. The number of international visitors to the UK has risen by 15% since 2025, with most people opting to stay within the country to avoid travel restrictions. However, there are also concerns about the impact of this trend on the UK’s tourism industry. If more people choose to stay closer to home, it could lead to a decline in demand for international tourism, which is still a significant part of the UK’s tourism industry. This could have wider-reaching implications for the economy, as the sector generates billions of pounds in revenue each year. Despite these concerns, the trend towards domestic tourism seems to be set to continue. Many Brits are rediscovering the beauty of their own country, from the stunning beaches of Cornwall to the historic cities of Tyne and Wear. As the UK’s tourism industry continues to evolve, it is increasingly likely that people will opt to explore the fascinating sites closest to home.
